title: Jev runs on Workers AI with the Cloudflare credential ticfac already holds
description: Superseded design (2026-09-28): x0k shipped the classifier on TypeSafe's own API — $TICFAC_JEV_API_KEY locally and a TYPESAFE_API_KEY Worker secret in the cloud — and this tick originally planned a ~/.ticfacrc home and a setup rung for that key. The operator has no TypeSafe key: Jev is served by Cloudflare Workers AI as typesafe/jev and billed to the operator's Cloudflare account (verified live: POST /accounts/<account>/ai/run with {"model":"typesafe/jev","input":{...}} answers result.result.answers). So there is no new credential to store or verify. Locally the classifier uses factory_cloudflare_api_token and the account in factory_gateway_url, both already in ~/.ticfacrc (env overrides TICFAC_JEV_API_TOKEN / TICFAC_JEV_ACCOUNT_ID / TICFAC_JEV_API_BASE for tests); in the cloud the factory Worker's /jev route runs typesafe/jev through the Workers AI REST API with its existing CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN secret, keeping the run-token exchange and kill switch, and is credit-billed so it needs no GATEWAY_ALLOWED_PROVIDERS opt-in. The TYPESAFE_API_KEY path is removed. 'ticfac doctor' and 'ticfac factory status' verify the credential by asking Jev one tiny question, which replaces the planned setup rung.
acceptance_criteria: The classifier needs no credential beyond the Cloudflare API token and account ~/.ticfacrc already holds (no contract key added); local and cloud paths call typesafe/jev on Workers AI and are tested against a fake Workers AI endpoint; the factory route no longer reads TYPESAFE_API_KEY; ticfac doctor and ticfac factory status report whether Jev answers with one live classification
closed_reason: Jev rewired to Workers AI (typesafe/jev) on the operator's existing Cloudflare token and account; doctor and factory status verify it live
